meta.a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA. Only tokens verified at a body contrast of 4.5:1 or better may be used as text.
meta.name: vinc-design
meta.note: The source of truth for the Vinc 'Signal' design system. base = the homepage and web Vinc theme (Home · Signal); the desktop tenant = the desktop application (Deep Signal). Operated dark first: the runtime default is data-theme=dark, while the generator is light-first and emits :root=light, so the consuming shell pins dark itself. Derivation: the Figma variables import of 2026-07-19, mapped by hand (document vinc.design.import-figma-variables-2026-07-19). Monochrome since 2026-09-24: dark is neutral black and surfaces and buttons are black, white or grey in both modes. Since 2026-09-25 one point colour per mode (point · point-text) marks where the eye should look: focus, selection, the graph focus and one emphasised phrase; it is never a surface. Otherwise only success, warning and danger keep a hue, plus the domain tint (a user toggle). The state notation (●◐○·≡≈) is kept alongside colour, never instead of it. Glow is for graph nodes only.
meta.ssot: Vinc graph: concept:token.* in vinc/design/tokens (snapshot Vinc:scripts/design/tokens.json)

notes.motion: Curves and durations. scripts/design/build_tokens.py inserts this group into every token CSS just before the Shape section. Values are shared by every skin. ease-out: entrances, exits, small UI (caret, press, hover lift). ease-in-out: something already on screen moving to a new place. ease-drawer: large surfaces (sidebar column, document pane, sheets) — the macOS drawer curve. ease-settle: strong deceleration for menus, cards and the modal growth in app/motion.ts. dur-in/dur-out/dur-panel are read by app/motion.ts and view-bundle.ts at runtime.
notes.topicJewels: Topic colour for the View marks, 3D glass bodies, the left tree dots and the node card mark: the jewel set of the homepage sculpture (ruby, sapphire, emerald, amber, amethyst), replacing the pale golden-angle tint on 2026-09-26 (see decision:topics-wear-the-homepage-jewels-2026-09-26). Always on, no toggle: a per-device toggle made the same graph look coloured on one machine and plain on another. Topics are sorted and take the jewels in order; past five, the set repeats with the hue turned 20 degrees per round, so topics on one screen do not share a colour until eleven. Dark uses a lifted set so a flat mark clears 5.5:1 on the background; light uses the deep set (the sculpture's own dark jewels, amber deepened) so every mark clears 3:1. The colour carries no meaning beyond telling topics apart: place says which topic.
notes.viewScene: Depth tiers for the View 3D mark, used only by the dark glow branch (app/src/surfaces/view3d.ts). These nodes are the canonical copy; the import documents vinc.design.import-figma-variables-* are only the record of the original import. Just three keys are consumed: fill, stroke and glowOpacity. glowRadius, edge and grid were removed on 2026-08-02 because no code read them (they were dead handles: changing the value changed nothing on screen). Values may be a {primitive} reference (resolved by scripts/design/build_tokens.py). Monochrome since 2026-09-24 except the focus and near tiers, which carry the dark point colour since 2026-09-25. Verified by Vinc/scripts/gate_contrast.py

props.note: Every token value of the Vinc design system, one concept:token.* node per token in vinc/design/tokens. This node holds the group order, the metadata, the group notes and the desktop tenant. scripts/design/pull_tokens.py reads them into the snapshot that the build reads.

$meta.name: desktop
$meta.note: The desktop application (Deep Signal) tenant, against the 2026-07 drafts. The dark palette converges deliberately on the same lineage as base(dark), one bloodline from logo to home to application, so there is no primitive override today. What makes the desktop distinct is not tokens but layout and components: the 232px sidebar, the constellation graph, glowing nodes, floating glass cards. When a divergence appears later (a brand font, a radius), add only the primitive leaf here. The View WebGL shades are generated by scripts/design/build_tokens.py from the viewScene tokens.
